narrative.overview:
The app is a binder. Sections are index tabs on the right edge, each with its own ink. Moving between pages turns a page. The work on the pages (checklists, card rows, label fields) sits on quiet surfaces. Neon is the binder's signage: the wordmark, the lit tab, the one button that moves you forward. It is not the wallpaper.

Because the people using it are both cataloguing at a desk and selling at a show table, the working surfaces are crisp and precise rather than playful. Dense lists, `text-sm` body, tight controls, keyboard-first. Personality comes from the wordmark, the neon and the voice of the copy, not from decorating the tools.

Two modes (NEO-356): Dark, the original black room with neon signs, and Light, theme 6 "Trapper Keeper Glo" (white sheets on a cool page, a hard neon offset, coloured tab edges, no glows). The person picks Light, Dark or System under Profile → Settings. Every colour is a role in app/theme.css set once per mode. Paper, card faces, the storefronts, the night shelf and the NEO-350 prototypes keep fixed colours.
keyCharacteristics: Three surface steps per mode: the page, a raised sheet, an input well.
One neon hue per binder section, shown on the lit tab (a glow in dark, a coloured edge in light).
Neon fills always carry black ink, in both modes.
In light each neon is deepened for use as text, to 4.5:1 on white.
The Neon display face appears only in the wordmark.
Index-tab navigation carries the binder metaphor; route changes are instant, with no page-turn transition.

rules.name: The Signage Rule
rules.body: Neon marks identity and action: the wordmark, the lit tab, the primary button, a status. Working surfaces stay on the neutral roles. If a screen reads as "neon everywhere", something is decorating instead of signalling.

rules.name: The Black Ink Rule
rules.body: Text on a neon fill is always black, in both modes. White on neon pink is 3.44:1 and on cyan 2.07:1; black is 6.1:1 or better on every hue. One ink keeps the buttons reading as one family.

rules.name: The Text Is Not The Fill Rule
rules.body: Neon used as text is text-neon-X-text, never text-neon-X. In dark they match (violet aside); in light the fill is under 2:1 on white.

rules.name: The One Hue Per Section Rule
rules.body: A section's colour is fixed by its tab (Dashboard green, Collection cyan, Inventory yellow, Admin amber, Print Shop teal, Profile violet). Don't borrow another section's hue for emphasis.

rules.name: The Role Not Step Rule
rules.body: Reach for the role that names the job (hover-raised, chip, selection-line), never a role that happens to have the right value in one mode (bg-rule-strong as a hover, bg-ink/10 as a chip). The second one breaks the other mode.

rules.name: The One Sign Rule
rules.body: The Neon face is the wordmark. It is never used for headings, buttons or body copy.

rules.name: The Four Weights Rule
rules.body: Lexend runs at 400 (body), 500 (labels, tabs), 600 (card and section titles) and 700 (page headings, numbers). Nothing lighter than 400, nothing heavier than 700.

rules.name: The Lit Means Active Rule
rules.body: A neon glow says "this is where you are" or "this is live". Never put a glow on a resting element for decoration.

rules.name: The Glow Not Fade Rule
rules.body: Neon text pulses its halo, never its opacity. `animate-pulse` on neon pink drops it to about 3:1 at the trough; the glow keeps the letters at full colour. One 12px halo, never stacked.

rules.name: The No Glow Alone Rule
rules.body: Light has no glows, so a selected or active state never rests on a glow alone: give it a line too (border-selection, ring-selection or selection-edge).

dos: **Do** paint with roles, and pick the role by its job, not by its value in one mode.
**Do** put black ink on every neon fill, in both modes.
**Do** keep each section in its tab's hue.
**Do** give a selected or active state a line as well as any glow or tint.
**Do** build every action button with NeonButton (primary green, secondary blue, tertiary violet, negative pink, each with an `outline` form); the lint rule refuses a neon-filled raw <button>.
**Do** honour `aria-disabled` on disabled buttons (dark dims the neon to 45%; light uses the neutral button fill).
**Do** print on white: print documents pin black on white and never load the app stylesheet; on-screen previews of paper use `bg-paper`.
**Do** look at every new screen in both modes, at desktop and phone widths.
donts: **Don't** use a `dark:` variant, a grey palette step, `text-white`/`bg-black`, or a raw hex in a class; the lint rule refuses them.
**Don't** branch on `[data-theme=light]` in a component's classes; add the missing role to theme.css, @theme and tokens.ts together.
**Don't** use white text on neon pink, cyan or green.
**Don't** fade neon text with `animate-pulse`; pulse the glow instead.
**Don't** use the Neon display face anywhere but the wordmark.
**Don't** put a glow on a resting element.
**Don't** use neon pink for anything but cancel, destructive and sign-out.
